newsitem.title: BELGIUM: RESEARCH ALERT - Solvay a 'hold' - Degroof.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Solvay a 'hold' - Degroof.

text.p: Belgian bank Degroof said in a research report dated June 18 it rated stock in Belgian chemicals and drugs group Solvay a 'hold', expecting the shares not to outperform in the months to come.

It said that at 22,300 francs the share was correctly valued relative to its major European peers, including commodity chemicals companies such as BASF and DSM and less cyclical groups such as Bayer and Akzo.
Solvay was down 325 francs at 21,700 on a generally weaker Brussels bourse on Thursday, continuing a correction begun on June 10 at 23,475.
Degroof said Solvay's performance might improve
- if there was positive news on the recovery of caustic soda prices, currently down 28 percent on last year's average;
- if concerns about worsening trading conditions for plastics in 1998 turned out to be exaggerated (margins are rising after 1996 prices were down 60 percent compared with 1995);
- if there was news on the approval of Solvay's flesinoxan drug (only expected in 1998).
